newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jordan's king and Netanyahu discuss Hebron deal.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king and Netanyahu discuss Hebron deal.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein held talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday on what a PLO official said was a new compromise proposal for a deal on Hebron and further Israeli withdrawals from the West Bank.

"I think everything is moving very, very well and I hope all these efforts will lead to a happy conclusion," the monarch told reporters before flying by helicopter to Tel Aviv from Gaza, where he met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"The king is carrying with him a compromise that has been discussed with the Americans, Egyptians and Arafat," the PLO official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters in Gaza. "It will be submitted to Netanyahu tonight."

U.S.-brokered talks between Israel and the PLO over self-rule for the town of Hebron have reached an impasse over the timing of three additional Israeli redeployments from mainly rural areas of the West Bank.
"The first phase of the redeployment has been agreed with the Israelis to start on February 28," the official said, disclosing the starting date for the first time.
"The three phases...will be completed within 12 months of the implementaton of the first phase, but not later than mid-1998," he said.

Israel proposes to complete the West Bank pullbacks by May 1999 and the United States has suggested mid-1998. The PLO had demanded Israel stick to a peace deal under which the withdrawals were to have been completed by September this year.
The official said Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat flew with King Hussein to Tel Aviv and that they would work all night drafting an agreement.
"If all is done, a (Arafat-Netanyahu) summit will be held on Monday," he said.

King Hussein, who has visited Israel several times since signing a 1994 peace treaty, had been widely expected to make the detour to see Netanyahu after his talks with Arafat in Palestinian self-ruled Gaza.
After the meeting between the king and Netanyahu was announced, a U.S. official said Washington's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross had cancelled his plans to leave the region on Sunday night.

Ross arrived three weeks ago to try again to wrap up a deal on Hebron, where some 400 Jews live amidst more than 100,000 Palestinians, but the negotiations took on a new dimension over the question of the additional Israeli redeployments.
Israel was due to have completed the Hebron handover 10 months ago but delayed the pullback after Moslem militant suicide bombers killed 59 people in the Jewish state last February and March.
Palestinian Planning Minister Nabil Shaath said King Hussein's "personal influence" on Israel might help sway Netanyahu.
But King Hussein, Israel's closest Arab friend in the months following the 1994 peace treaty, has distanced himself from Netanyahu over policies that include support for Jewish settlement expansion.
